entries.definition: To cleanse is to remove the defilement that bars proper contact, approach, or use; clean describes what is free of that defilement and fit for its permitted place. Uncleanness may be physical, ceremonial, or moral and does not always mean guilt: childbirth, marital relations, and touching the dead all make unclean without being called sin. Cleansing removes what makes a vessel unfit; sanctification places the cleansed vessel under a holy claim and appointed use.
entries.common_view: Commonly treated either as hygiene and obsolete ritual regulation, or as a synonym for moral purity and holiness.
entries.citations: (Lev 10:10; 12:2; 15:18; Num 19:11; Ps 51:2, 10; Eph 5:26; 1 John 1:7, 9) · see Uncommon Sanctification, Justification, and Cleanliness

entries.definition: To judge, declare, or demonstrate a person, word, deed, or cause right against a question or charge; the opposite is to condemn. God answers the charge against the sinner by grace through Christ, forgiving rather than renaming ungodliness righteousness. Deeds may vindicate a claimed faith, but they cannot purchase the Judge's mercy or place God in debt.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught in Protestant theology: God's once-for-all legal declaration that a believer is righteous through Christ's imputed righteousness, received by faith apart from works.
entries.citations: (Deut 25:1; Prov 17:15; Matt 11:19; Luke 7:29; Rom 3:24-26; 4:4-8; 8:33; Jas 2:21-25) · see Uncommon Sanctification, Justification, and Cleanliness, and The End of the Law for Paul's law, works, wages, and debt vocabulary

entries.definition: To cause, appoint, or acknowledge as holy — removing someone or something from common status, placing it under an owner's claim for an appointed purpose, and treating or preparing it accordingly. God sanctifies by claiming for Himself and fitting for His use; people sanctify God and His Name by treating and displaying Him as holy. Moral cleansing and obedient living fit a person to that holy calling, but they are not the word's entire meaning.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: God's progressive work of inward renewal, by which believers die more and more to sin and live in righteousness.
entries.citations: (Ex 13:2; Num 8:17; Isa 8:13; Ezek 36:23; John 10:36; 17:19; 1 Cor 7:14; 1 Thess 4:3-7; 2 Tim 2:21; Heb 10:10, 29) · see Uncommon Sanctification, Justification, and Cleanliness
